original_question: For the three-machine precedence-constrained scheduling problem P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Open Problem 6: the paper's official question asks whether P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem almost exactly: it has the correct scheduling notation P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max, the correct parameter (the width of the precedence partial order), and the correct complexity-theoretic target (fixed-parameter tractability). This is precisely the question singled out in Section 4.2 as Open Problem 6.
missing_details: State explicitly that P3 means three parallel identical machines.
State explicitly that the schedule is nonpreemptive; this is the paper's default unless 'pmtn' is written in the middle field.
Define p_j=1 as meaning every job has unit processing time.
Define the width parameter as the maximum size of an antichain in the partial order induced by the precedence constraints.
Spell out that the question asks for fixed-parameter tractability with respect to width alone, i.e. an algorithm with running time f(w)·n^{O(1)} where w is the width.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, unpack C_max as minimizing the completion time of the last job, or equivalently computing an optimal minimum-makespan schedule.
Clarify that the partial order is the one on the jobs induced by the precedence constraints, not some other graph width notion.
refined_question: Is the nonpreemptive three-machine parallel-identical scheduling problem P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized solely by the width w of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints, where p_j=1 for every job j and w is the maximum size of an antichain of jobs; equivalently, is there an algorithm running in time f(w)·n^{O(1)} that computes an optimal minimum-makespan schedule for such instances?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper-faithful formulation. The exact target is Open Problem 6 in Section 4.2, and the nearby context there defines width as the size of a largest antichain and explains why this parameterization is natural for precedence-constrained makespan scheduling. To make the question fully stand-alone, I only unpacked the Graham notation using the paper's preliminaries: P denotes parallel identical machines, 'prec' denotes precedence constraints, p_j=1 denotes unit processing times, and nonpreemption is the default because no 'pmtn' qualifier is present. I also made the meaning of fixed-parameter tractability explicit via the paper's Section 2.2 definition. No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree condition, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' quantifier is relevant to this scheduling problem.
